item.title: Dallas Trash Trucks Are Scoring Homes With AI — 20,000 Flags, 57 Citations
item.description: Dallas put AI cameras on 50 sanitation trucks, and a new Dallas Morning News analysis says the system photographed more than 20,000 potential code concerns in four months while producing 57 citations at 34 properties. Puck and Kore unpack the strange collision of municipal efficiency, privacy, algorithmic scoring, human review and public trust—and why marketers should pay attention whenever invisible automation starts making visible decisions about people. Follow this podcast and @socialwithrob on Instagram for more marketing secrets.

item.title: Congress Turns Up the Pressure on Russia as Chips, AI Safety and Climate Spending Shift
item.description: Congress advances a sweeping Russia sanctions package as global business keeps moving: Applied Materials commits $5 billion to India, OpenAI discloses troubling model behavior and Google signs its largest carbon-removal deal yet. We break down what these stories reveal about pressure, trust, infrastructure and the messages brands inherit from the systems around them. item.title: Google Dodged an Ad-Tech Breakup — But Its Advertising Rules Are About to Change | Nightcap
item.description: Google escaped a forced breakup of its ad-tech business, but a federal judge ordered changes designed to open its advertising markets to more competition. Plus: the Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time since 2023, the SEC proposed a major shift in shareholder-vote oversight, and Dallas is becoming a proving ground for a cheaper drone-delivery model. item.title: The Fed Just Made Attention More Expensive | Evening
item.description: The Federal Reserve raises rates for the first time since 2023, OpenAI pushes sponsored agents deeper into ChatGPT, the SEC proposes a major shift in shareholder-vote oversight, and Google makes its biggest carbon-removal deal yet. Puck and Kore decode what higher capital costs, conversational commerce, corporate accountability and AI infrastructure mean for marketers. item.title: Ads Just Learned How to Talk Back
item.description: OpenAI is testing business-sponsored AI agents, AI adoption is racing ahead of obvious productivity gains, and forecasts for autonomous agents are getting enormous. Puck and Kore break down what conversational advertising could change, why marketers need better measurement instead of more AI theater, and why trust, taste, judgment and machine-readable brand truth may become more valuable as execution gets cheaper.
